paper_title: Searching for Dark Matter with a Superconducting Qubit
notes: Hidden-photon (dark photon) dark matter search with a superconducting-qubit photon counter in a 6.011 GHz (24.86 ueV) cavity. Headline result: kinetic mixing chi = epsilon <= 1.68e-15 excluded at 90% CL on resonance (m_gammaprime c^2 = hbar omega_s), assuming rho_DM=0.4 GeV/cm^3 (not rescaled). Reported chi=epsilon directly (paper quotes epsilon, the kinetic mixing angle; never chi^2). Curve = the central resonance spike traced from the purple exclusion region of Fig 4 inset (dp_limplot_V6.pdf, vector paths); depth anchored to the text value epsilon=1.68e-15 (log-baseline calibration gave 2.1e-15, ~20% high). The search is single-frequency: the deep exclusion is a very narrow spike (deep part within a few kHz / <1e-11 eV of 6.011 GHz; -3dB at 3 kHz). Fig-4 inset also shows a comb of much weaker (epsilon~1e-9..1e-10) off-resonance teeth at odd multiples of the dispersive shift 2chi=1.13 MHz; these are not the headline limit and are omitted. Mass from m=h*f, f=6.011 GHz -> 2.4859e-5 eV.
